Name: Nguyen Hue Walking Street
Area: Nguyen Hue Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Nguyen Hue Walking Street is one of the most famous and vibrant destinations in the heart of Saigon. Stretching from the City Hall to the Saigon River, it offers a spacious and modern pedestrian area surrounded by cafes, restaurants, and historical landmarks. The street attracts both locals and tourists who come to relax, enjoy the open-air atmosphere, and watch dynamic street performances. During weekends and holidays, it becomes a lively gathering spot filled with music, laughter, and art shows. At night, colorful LED lights and fountain displays create a dazzling scene. Visitors can take photos, try local snacks, or simply immerse themselves in the city’s youthful and energetic vibe. It’s truly a must-visit place to experience the modern spirit of Ho Chi Minh City.

Name: Ben Thanh Market
Area: Ben Thanh, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Ben Thanh Market is one of the most iconic landmarks of Saigon, representing the city’s vibrant culture and long history. First established in the 18th century, it has been relocated and rebuilt several times before reaching its current location in 1914. The market is easily recognized by its classic French-style architecture and the iconic clock tower that stands proudly at the main entrance. Inside, visitors can find a wide variety of products, from traditional handicrafts and souvenirs to clothing, spices, and local delicacies. The market is also a great place to taste authentic Vietnamese street food and experience the daily life of Saigonese people. Both locals and tourists come here not only to shop but also to enjoy the bustling and colorful atmosphere. Ben Thanh Market remains a timeless symbol of Ho Chi Minh City’s charm and cultural identity.

Name: Bui Vien Walking Street
Area: Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Bui Vien Walking Street is one of the most famous and energetic “sleepless” areas in Saigon, known for its lively and youthful atmosphere. Located in the city center, it attracts both locals and international visitors who come to enjoy its endless nightlife. The street is lined with bustling bars, pubs, cafes, and restaurants offering everything from local dishes to international cuisine. Street performers, live music, and dazzling neon lights make the area come alive after sunset. Visitors can sit at a roadside bar, enjoy a cold drink, and watch the vibrant flow of people passing by. Bui Vien is also a popular place for backpackers seeking affordable fun and cultural exchange. With its mix of entertainment, food, and nightlife, it truly represents the dynamic and modern spirit of Saigon.

Name: Notre-Dame Cathedral of Saigon
Area: Paris Commune Square, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Saigon Notre-Dame Cathedral is one of the most iconic landmarks of Ho Chi Minh City, rich in history and culture. Built in the late 19th century in a Romanesque and Gothic architectural style by the French, the cathedral stands out with its twin bell towers and distinctive red bricks imported from Marseille. Beyond its religious significance, it serves as a popular tourist attraction that draws both locals and visitors worldwide. Although currently under restoration, the cathedral remains a symbol of timeless beauty and an unmissable destination in the heart of Saigon.

Name: Bach Dang Pier
Area: No. 1, Ton Duc Thang Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Bach Dang Wharf is a vibrant riverside park and pier located along the Saigon River, attracting both locals and tourists. It is an ideal spot to enjoy the city’s scenery, breathe in the fresh air, and admire the stunning view as the sun sets over the skyline. Beyond its modern charm and lively atmosphere, the wharf holds deep historical significance, symbolizing the nation’s heroic victories and resilient spirit. Today, it also serves as the starting point for high-speed boat trips to Vung Tau and other scenic river tours. Visitors can take a leisurely walk, capture beautiful photos, savor riverside cuisine, or enjoy a relaxing night cruise on the river.

Name: Nguyen Van Binh Book Street
Area: Nguyen Van Binh Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Nguyen Van Binh Book Street is a unique cultural attraction in the heart of Saigon, drawing both locals and tourists. Lined with lush trees, this charming street is a “book paradise” featuring dozens of stalls from well-known publishers and bookstores. It’s not only a haven for book lovers but also a relaxing space for coffee, reading, and cultural exchange. Visitors can stroll around, take photos, read books, or simply enjoy the peaceful atmosphere amid the bustling city. The street also hosts regular exhibitions, events, and children’s activities that promote the love of reading throughout the community.

Name: Vincom Dong Khoi
Area: 72 Le Thanh Ton Street and 45A Ly Tu Trong Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Vincom Center Dong Khoi is one of Ho Chi Minh City’s most luxurious shopping malls, located in the heart of District 1. It features over 150 top fashion, dining, and entertainment brands, creating the perfect space for shopping, dining, and relaxation. Visitors can enjoy international cuisine at Haidilao, San Fu Lou, or Sushi Hokkaido Sachi, and sip coffee at Starbucks or Cong Café. The modern CGV cinema and Vuivuiland play zone make it an ideal destination for families and friends. With its elegant design and premium services, Vincom Dong Khoi stands as a symbol of modern lifestyle in the vibrant heart of Saigon.

Name: Ho Chi Minh City Post Office
Area: No. 2, Paris Commune Square Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Saigon Central Post Office is one of Ho Chi Minh City’s most iconic architectural landmarks, built between 1886 and 1891 in an eclectic style designed by French architect Marie-Alfred Foulhoux. The building harmoniously blends Western architecture with Eastern decorative details. Inside, it features impressive iron arches and two hand-painted historical maps. Gustave Eiffel was involved in the early design phase. After several restorations, most notably in 2014, the post office remains a popular tourist attraction and a symbol of the city’s colonial heritage.

Name: Independence Palace
Area: No. 135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: The Independence Palace, also known as the Reunification Palace, is a famous historical landmark in Ho Chi Minh City. Designed by architect Ngo Viet Thu and completed in 1966, it once served as the workplace of the President of South Vietnam before 1975. The building features a modern architectural style harmoniously blended with traditional Vietnamese elements. On April 30, 1975, Liberation Army tanks entered the palace, marking the reunification of the country. Today, the palace is a national special historical site and a popular attraction for both local and international visitors.

Name: Saigon Garden
Area: 99 Nguyen Hue Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Saigon Garden is a modern commercial and entertainment complex often described as a “green oasis in the heart of Saigon.” It stands out for its unique architecture that blends nature with a contemporary urban style. Inside, visitors can find a variety of fashion boutiques, cafés, fine-dining restaurants, and relaxing spaces. With its vibrant atmosphere, lush greenery, and countless photo-worthy corners, Saigon Garden has become a favorite destination for both locals and tourists. It’s the perfect spot for shopping, dining, and enjoying leisure time right in the center of the city.

Name: September 23rd Park
Area: Pham Ngu Lao Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: September 23rd Park is one of Ho Chi Minh City’s most popular attractions, drawing both locals and tourists. Covered in lush greenery, the park offers a peaceful escape amid the city’s vibrant energy. Visitors can take a walk, exercise, or simply relax and enjoy the scenery. Beneath the park lies Taka Plaza and Asiana Food Town — a shopping and dining paradise. During festivals, it becomes a lively venue for cultural events, music, and fairs. It’s the perfect place to experience the youthful and dynamic spirit of Saigon.

Name: Vee Ayy Food
Area: 345/84 Tran Hung Dao Street, Cau Kho Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: This article by Quán Số highlights their partnership with the Vee Ayy Food Restaurant chain, a popular dining spot trending among young people. The restaurant stands out for its luxurious, palace-like interior, offering many "Instagrammable" photo corners, along with a diverse menu of high-quality, reasonably priced European and Asian dishes. The chain currently operates two branches in Ho Chi Minh City. Quán Số is proud to provide their DRS Manager Sales Management Software along with other solutions like DRS Staff (remote ordering) and QS Admin (remote management) to help Vee Ayy Food run operations and serve customers optimally. Quán Số pledges to continue developing the best possible solutions for business management.

Name: miya sushi & bbq
Area: 150/43A Nguyen Trai Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Miya Sushi & BBQ is a well-known Japanese restaurant chain offering a unique fusion of the refined flavors of fresh Sushi and Sashimi with the appeal of tableside BBQ dishes. The restaurant features a cozy and elegant atmosphere, reflecting the culture of the Land of the Rising Sun, making it perfect for dates, family gatherings, and friends' meetups. Miya's menu is highly diverse, ranging from traditional Sushi rolls, Ramen, and Udon to Japanese rice sets and BBQ items marinated in special sauces. With its focus on fresh, high-quality ingredients and meticulous preparation, Miya Sushi & BBQ is an ideal destination for Saigon's food enthusiasts seeking an authentic and memorable Japanese culinary experience at a reasonable price point.

Name: My Son Quang Noodles
Area: 38B Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: My Son Quang Noodles is a popular spot in District 1, celebrated for its authentic Quang-style noodles from Central Vietnam. The restaurant draws diners with its soft, white rice noodles bathed in a minimal yet rich and flavorful broth, seasoned with a distinct recipe. The bowls are generously filled with diverse toppings, most commonly shrimp and pork, free-range chicken, or snakehead fish, served with roasted peanuts, fragrant fried shallots, and crispy rice crackers. The restaurant's ambiance is typically simple, airy, with warm tones, subtly evoking the rustic charm of the ancient town of Hội An. Mì Quảng Mỹ Sơn is an excellent choice for anyone seeking the traditional flavors of Quảng Nam right in the heart of bustling Saigon.

Name: Back of the Bike Tours – Ho Chi Minh City Food Tours
Area: 72 Le Thanh Ton Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Back of the Bike Tours is one of the leading companies in HCMC, specializing in food and cultural tours conducted via motorbikes. The unique concept has guests riding pillion with a local guide, venturing deep into hidden alleys, residential areas, and "secret" eateries that tourists would rarely discover on their own. The tours are highly praised for their safety, friendly staff, and ability to help visitors authentically experience the vibrant pulse of Saigon traffic. The meticulously curated food menu features a blend of classic and unique dishes, ensuring a complete and exciting culinary journey through the flavors of Saigon.

Name: Chu Chen's Rib Porridge & Char Siu Rice
Area: 281 Nguyen Trai Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Chu Chen's Rib Porridge and Char Siu Rice is a popular Taiwanese-style food chain, best known for its unique Taiwanese Rib Porridge. The porridge is characterized by its exceptionally smooth, velvety texture, cooked until creamy, and served with tender baby ribs and century eggs or various other toppings. Additionally, the restaurant offers delicious Char Siu Rice, featuring intensely marinated and roasted char siu pork prepared with a secret recipe, accompanied by a signature sauce and soft rice. With its novel, authentic street food flavor from Taiwan, Chu Chen is an ideal destination for those looking for a different taste and wishing to enjoy a hot, nutritious meal right in the heart of Saigon.

Name: Bento Dino
Area: 134/3/1 Bui Thi Xuan Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Bento Dino is a popular eatery in the heart of District 1, well-known for its Crispy Fried Chicken Rice and affordable, high-quality office lunch options. The restaurant attracts numerous students and office workers by blending traditional Vietnamese flavors with a modern, clean presentation, resembling the convenient Bento box style. Their signature fried chicken is specially prepared, featuring a golden, crispy skin served alongside dry, fragrant, and non-greasy fried rice grains. Bento Dino also stands out with a diverse menu, including pork chop, stir-fried beef, and fish, along with frequent appealing promotions. It is an ideal choice for a quick, delicious, and fulfilling lunch.

Name: Hua Wu Lou
Area: 83B Bui Thi Xuan Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Hua Wu Lou (Dimsum Street) is a popular restaurant chain featuring a distinctive Chinese street-food and restaurant style, specializing in delicious Dimsum dishes. The restaurant attracts diners with its diverse menu, ranging from classics like Shrimp Dumplings, Siu Mai, and Steamed Chicken Feet with Black Bean Sauce to unique items such as Baked Crab Shell with Cheese or Hand-held Shrimp Vermicelli. The Dimsum here is praised for retaining its authentic flavor, with fresh, thin wrappers and generous fillings, always served piping hot. Hua Wu Lou also offers convenient lunch sets, perfect for office workers. With a cozy interior featuring traditional decor, it is an ideal spot to savor the best of Hong Kong cuisine at a reasonable price point in central Saigon.

Name: Di Nam Sa Dec's Hu Tieu Sa Dec and Banh Tam
Area: 166 Bui Thi Xuan Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, VIetnam
Overview: Di Nam Sa Dec's Hu Tieu Sa Dec and Banh Tam is a renowned eatery in District 1 that embodies the authentic culinary spirit of the Mekong Delta, specializing in two famous dishes: Sa Dec Noodle Soup and Banh Tam. Their Sa Dec Hủ Tiếu is beloved for its distinctively chewy yet soft noodles, clear and naturally sweet broth made from simmered bones, and fresh toppings. Conversely, Bánh Tằm Bì is a unique dish featuring thick, chewy rice noodles, finely sliced pork skin, and spring rolls, topped with rich coconut milk and a sweet-and-sour fish sauce. The shop attracts diners with its genuine, rustic Sa Dec flavors, creating the feeling of dining right in the Mekong Delta region. Di Nam Sa Dec is the perfect place to experience the richness of Southern Vietnamese cuisine.

Name: Pho Hien 1985
Area: 269A Nguyen Trai Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Pho Hien 1985 is a time-honored traditional Pho restaurant, famous in District 1, having served patrons for decades. The shop is beloved for faithfully preserving the traditional Northern Pho flavor, featuring a clear, naturally sweet broth simmered from beef bones for hours, subtly fragrant with herbs and spices. Pho Hien specializes in various beef Pho options, ranging from rare beef, flank, and brisket to the premium beef shank (loi rua). The rice noodles are soft and tender, the beef slices are fresh and high-quality, served with crispy quay (fried dough) and fresh herbs. Pho Hien 1985 is not just a place to eat, but a keeper of traditional culinary culture, making it an ideal choice for anyone seeking an authentic and comforting bowl of Pho.

Name: Ancient Hue Beef Noodle Soup
Area: 148 Bis Le Thi Rieng Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Bun Bo Hue Xua is a popular restaurant chain that brings the traditional flavors of Bun Bo Hue (Hue Beef Noodle Soup) to the heart of Saigon. The eatery is favored by patrons for its high-quality bowls that perfectly capture the richness and spicy zest characteristic of Hue cuisine. The broth is slow-simmered, fragrant with lemongrass and fermented shrimp paste, creating a distinctive and memorable taste. The generous bowls are loaded with various toppings, including beef, pork hock, crab paste patties, and blood pudding, catering to all preferences. With a clean, cozy atmosphere and affordable prices, Bun Bo Hue Xua is a frequent stop for both locals and tourists seeking an authentic and comforting taste of the ancient Imperial city.

Name: Cong Quynh Mixed Rice Paper
Area: 125 Cong Quynh Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Cong Quynh Mixed Rice Paper (Banh Trang Tron Cong Quynh) is one of the most famous and longest-running street food stalls in District 1, often dubbed a culinary "paradise" for Saigon's youth and office workers. The popular snack is a delightful mix of textures and flavors, centered around chewy strips of rice paper. It’s characterized by the perfect balance of the sourness from shredded green mango, the savory richness of dried beef and quail eggs, and a spicy kick from chili paste. The stall's secret lies in its generous, flavorful toppings and the fragrant aroma from fried shallots and roasted peanuts. Located on Cong Quynh street, this spot perfectly embodies the creative, delicious, and highly affordable street food culture that Saigon is famous for, making it an essential local experience.

Name: Nguyen Hue Flower Street
Area: 6 Nguyen Hue Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Nguyen Hue Flower Street (Duong Hoa Nguyen Hue) is an annual floral art event that transforms the Nguyen Hue Pedestrian Street in District 1 into a vibrant, giant flower park every Lunar New Year (Tet) holiday. This installation has become a new cultural symbol of Ho Chi Minh City since 2004. The Flower Street is designed with a different theme each year, usually featuring the corresponding Zodiac animal (e.g., the Dragon for the Year of the Dragon) and conveying messages of reunion, peace, and prosperity. The street typically opens to the public for about seven days (from the 28th day of the Lunar December to the 5th day of Tet) and attracts millions of visitors who come to admire and photograph the stunning floral displays, making it an indispensable part of Saigon's festive atmosphere.

Name: Ngo Nho Pho Nho's Bun Dau
Area: 158 Pasteur Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Bun Dau Ngo Nho Pho Nho is a well-known eatery in District 1, faithfully bringing the distinct flavors of Hanoi's street food to Saigon. The restaurant is famous for its generous and fresh platter of Bun Dau Mam Tom (Rice Vermicelli with Tofu and Fermented Shrimp Paste), which includes rice vermicelli, hot crispy fried tofu, thit chan gio luoc (boiled pork knuckle), cha com (green rice flake sausage), and pork sausage. The crucial highlight is the Mam Tom (fermented shrimp paste) dipping sauce, expertly mixed with a balanced blend of sour, spicy, and sweet flavors. The restaurant's ambiance is cozy, recreating the feel of Hanoi's ancient small alleys and small streets (Ngo Nho, Pho Nho). This is an ideal choice for food lovers seeking authentic Northern Vietnamese cuisine.

Name: Ba Son Harbour Park
Area: 2 Ton Duc Thang Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Ba Son Harbour Park is located on the historic site of the former Ba Son Shipyard, right along the Saigon River in central District 1. Regarded as a "new public square" and a green riverside space, the park is a key component of the Grand Marina Saigon and Vinhomes Golden River complex. It offers a tranquil, green oasis, providing a complete escape from the urban hustle. The park is renowned for its spectacular panoramic views overlooking the Thu Thiem Peninsula and the surrounding skyscrapers of District 1. Ba Son Harbour Park is an ideal spot for catching the sunrise, morning exercise, and serves as a picturesque, romantic check-in location, marking the convergence of historical heritage and modern urban architecture.

Name: Kim’s Tavern
Area: 20 Huynh Thuc Khang Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Kim's Tavern is a vibrant bar located in the heart of District 1, known as a "hidden gem" that harmoniously blends a lively atmosphere with exceptional service. The tavern is highly favored for its warm, engaging ambiance and its friendly, attentive staff. Kim's Tavern offers a diverse selection of drinks, ranging from beautifully crafted cocktails to various beers and spirits. The venue often hosts activities and engaging interactions with its patrons, creating a relaxed yet exciting environment. It is an ideal nightlife spot for socializing, unwinding, and experiencing the vibrant energy of Saigon after dark.

Name: Dao Snail
Area: 212B/D28 Nguyen Trai Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Oc Dao is one of the most famous and longest-running snail and seafood shops in District 1, having even earned recognition in the prestigious MICHELIN Selected list. The eatery draws crowds with its extensive menu of fresh Oc (snails and shellfish), cooked in various signature Saigon styles. Famous dishes include Oc Huong rang muoi ot (Sweet Snails stir-fried with chili salt), Oc Mo xao bo toi (Fat Snails with butter and garlic), and So Diep nuong mo hanh (Grilled Scallops with scallion oil). Oc Dao retains its loyal customer base due to its intensely flavorful dishes, meticulously prepared sauces, and its characteristic sizzling cast iron pan that keeps the food hot. With its bustling, casual atmosphere, it is the perfect place to experience Saigon's vibrant street food culture after dark.

Name: The Kitchen of Luc Tinh
Area: 37 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Bep Nha Luc Tinh is a renowned restaurant in District 1 specializing in traditional Southern Vietnamese cuisine (from the historic Six Provinces). The restaurant features a spacious and airy ambiance, completely separated from the street noise, with a rustic design that strongly evokes the Mekong Delta region, including a water model and outdoor seating. The menu is diverse, focusing on authentic, simple dishes such as kho quet (caramelized fish sauce dip), canh chua (sour soup), and lau mam (fermented fish hotpot), all prepared with true regional flavors. With its elegant and polite atmosphere, Bep Nha Luc Tinh is an ideal venue for family gatherings, business meetings, or hosting international guests to experience the rich and authentic taste of Vietnamese cuisine.

Name: Quan Ngon 138 – Vietnamese Food
Area: 138 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Quan Ngon 138 is a prominent restaurant located in central District 1, serving as a hub for the culinary essence of all three regions of Vietnam (North, Central, and South). With a vast menu featuring over 300 dishes, it is an ideal spot to sample everything from Northern Pho and Bun Cha, Central Mi Quang and Cao Lau, to Southern Banh Xeo and Com Tam (Broken Rice). The restaurant's atmosphere is designed to be cozy and evocative, recreating the look of traditional old streets and rural markets, offering a nostalgic and familiar feel. Quan Ngon 138 caters not only to casual dining but also provides private rooms and party areas with karaoke, making it perfect for business entertaining, banquets, and family gatherings.

Name: Elixir Lounge Bar
Area: 28B/1 Ngo Van Nam Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Elixir Lounge Bar is a stylish and prominent lounge located in central District 1 (near the Le Thanh Ton Japanese Quarter). The bar attracts a diverse crowd of locals and international tourists, thanks to its blend of a luxurious, intimate setting and a vibrant musical atmosphere. Elixir consistently updates its music trends, featuring genres like House, EDM, and Top 40, supported by a state-of-the-art sound and lighting system that creates a high-energy environment. The bar offers a wide variety of drinks, including cocktails and bottled spirits, alongside various fun entertainment options. With its professional and friendly staff, Elixir is an ideal spot to fully experience the dynamic, upscale nightlife of Saigon.

Name: The Alley Cocktail Bar & Kitchen
Area: 63/8 Pasteur Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: The Alley Cocktail Bar & Kitchen is a distinctive bar famous for its location, hidden away in a quiet alley in central District 1. The venue adopts a speakeasy style, with its interior designed to be classic and intimate, utilizing dark wood and soft yellow lighting. The Alley attracts cocktail enthusiasts with its creative, subtly mixed, and highly personalized drink menu. Beyond quality cocktails, the Kitchen menu offers unique Asian and European appetizers and main courses, suitable for an intimate dinner. The Alley is the perfect choice for those seeking a tranquil retreat, eager to escape the hustle and bustle and enjoy the art of cocktail making in a private setting.

Name: Layla – Eatery & Bar
Area: Second Floor, 63 Dong Du Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Layla – Eatery & Bar is a stylish and popular bar and restaurant located on the second floor of an old apartment building in central District 1 (near Dong Khoi and Dong Du streets). The venue features an Industrial Chic style blended with a touch of vintage charm, creating a cozy, unpretentious, and highly chill-out atmosphere. Founded by an Australian bartender, Layla is renowned for its high-quality, creative cocktails and a solid menu of tapas and Mediterranean-inspired bar bites. Thanks to its prime location, the bar offers large windows overlooking the bustling streets below, making it an ideal choice for anyone seeking a relaxed space to enjoy excellent drinks and intimate conversations.

Name: Burger King Pham Ngu Lao
Area: 223-225 Pham Ngu Lao Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Burger King Pham Ngu Lao is a prominent branch of the famous American fast-food chain, located right in the heart of the bustling "Backpacker Area" in District 1. The restaurant is renowned for its signature Whopper – a flame-grilled beef burger that sets it apart from competitors. Beyond its diverse range of beef and chicken burgers, Burger King also serves popular sides like crispy french fries and notably offers free soda refills (subject to current policy). With its comfortable seating, late operating hours, and a prime location overlooking the park, this is an ideal pit stop for both tourists and young locals craving quick and satisfying fast food.

Name: Kasen Omakase
Area: 101 Le Thi Rieng Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Kasen Omakase is a prominent Omakase restaurant in Saigon, offering a high-end Japanese dining experience based on the philosophy of "Trust the Chef" (Omakase). The restaurant operates without a fixed menu; instead, the dishes are determined by the chef based on the freshest seasonal ingredients, ensuring a unique and constantly evolving experience. Kasen stands out by blending classic Japanese techniques with innovative, modern (fusion) creations such as Foie Gras Nigiri or Sashimi marinated with Truffle oil. The dining space is cozy and refined, often featuring a counter where guests can directly interact with the chef, making the meal an artistic and surprising culinary journey.

Name: Bo By Butterman
Area: 67 Le Thi Rieng Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Bo By Butterman is a popular dessert shop, especially favored by Saigon's youth for its unique handmade pastries and affordable prices. The shop immediately captivates customers with the fragrant aroma of butter filling the air and its wide variety of sweets. Highlights include colorful Marshmallows with various intriguing fillings, Cookies with a balanced, non-overly sweet texture, and dense Brownies. Although the space is small, the interior is charmingly decorated, creating a cozy and relaxing atmosphere. Bo By Butterman is an ideal spot to either take away or enjoy desserts like their famous cookies along with drinks such as Matcha Latte or coffee.

Name: Sai Gon Oi Coffee
Area: 42 Nguyen Hue Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Sai Gon Oi Coffee is a familiar and beloved cafe often situated in prime locations in central District 1. The shop stands out with its refined, modern design and spacious balcony offering stunning views of the vibrant Saigon streets. With its open, light-filled atmosphere, the cafe creates a comfortable and relaxing environment, perfectly suited for those seeking a moment of "slow living" amidst the city bustle. The menu is varied, ranging from traditional Vietnamese coffees to refreshing fruit teas, catering to diverse tastes. Sai Gon Oi is an ideal place to enjoy quality coffee and fully appreciate the dynamic, yet romantic, beauty of the city.

Name: Whisfee Coffee
Area: 14 Ton That Dam Street, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Whisfee Café is a distinctive coffee shop famous for being a hidden gem tucked away on the first floor of an old apartment building at 14 Ton That Dam in District 1. The cafe boasts a retro style blended with European vintage aesthetics, featuring dark wood, leather chairs, and warm lighting, resembling a small European bar or an old study room. Whisfee is highly favored for its tranquil, relaxing atmosphere, providing a peaceful escape from the bustling streets, making it perfect for reading or quiet conversations. The menu offers high-quality coffees and teas, including signature drinks like Egg Coffee with Rum and Coconut Coffee, and features a large window area overlooking the street.

Name: Lost – Drink & Chill
Area: 71/5 Mac Thi Buoi Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Lost – Drink & Chill is a popular bar favored by Saigon's youth, located in central District 1, known for perfectly blending a relaxed, chilling atmosphere with a lively, exciting environment. The venue is designed to be cozy and intimate yet spacious enough to accommodate both small and large groups. Lost offers a diverse drink menu, ranging from creative signature cocktails to strong spirits, beers, and non-alcoholic options. Notably, the music is a highlight, with frequent appearances by DJs playing EDM, House, and Hip-hop, alongside more relaxed acoustic live music on weekdays. With its unique space, quality beverages, and reasonable prices, it is an ideal nightlife destination for socializing and unwinding.

Name: Hoang’s Kitchen
Area: 45 Thu Khoa Huan Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Hoang's Kitchen is a prominent Vietnamese restaurant near Ben Thanh Market, known for its superb fusion of traditional cuisine and extensive high-quality vegan options. The restaurant captivates diners with a diverse menu where dishes are delicately prepared, offering rich, balanced flavors and beautiful presentation. Hoang's Kitchen is highly praised for its exceptional vegan offerings, such as Pho chay (Vegan Pho) and the vegetable spring rolls, often surprising even meat-eaters. The cozy, spacious environment, coupled with friendly, energetic, and English-speaking staff, makes Hoang's Kitchen an ideal spot for both locals and international visitors looking to experience the best of Vietnamese gastronomy.

Name: Saigon Zoo
Area: 2 Nguyen Binh Khiem Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City , Vietnam
Overview: Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens (known locally as So Thu or The Zoo) is one of the world's oldest continually operating zoological parks, established in 1864. Located right in the heart of District 1, it is often referred to as the city’s "green lung," offering a vast, fresh escape from the urban bustle. Covering nearly 17 hectares, the venue currently conserves over 1,300 animals across 125 species and more than 2,500 trees spanning 360 species, including many rare varieties. More than just an amusement spot, the Saigon Zoo and Botanical Gardens serves as a vital center for conservation, education, and research on biodiversity.

Name: Tao Dan Park
Area: Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Tao Dan Park is one of the largest and oldest parks in District 1, widely known as the "green lung" of Saigon. It features a dense concentration of greenery, including many hundred-year-old trees, creating an airy and peaceful sanctuary away from the city noise. The park is a popular spot for morning exercises and is famously the venue for the traditional Hoi Hoa Xuan (Spring Flower Festival) held before the Lunar New Year (Tet). Within the park's grounds are significant historical landmarks such as the Temple dedicated to the Hung Kings and the ancient Lam family tomb area, establishing Tao Dan not just as a place for relaxation but also as a site rich in the city's cultural and historical heritage.

Name: Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts
Area: 97A Pho Duc Chinh Street, Nguyen Thai Binh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: The Ho Chi Minh City Museum of Fine Arts is one of Vietnam's largest and most significant museums, renowned for both its extensive art collection and its distinctive architecture. The main building, constructed in the 1920s, features an elegant blend of French colonial and Asian architectural styles (noted for its tiled roofs, arched windows, and striking yellow facade). The museum displays over 21,000 artworks spanning centuries, from ancient sculptures of the Oc Eo and Champa cultures to modern paintings and sculptures by famous Vietnamese artists. This site serves not only as a cultural landmark but also as an "Instagrammable" location due to its classic, visually impressive beauty.

Name: Little Japan Town Saigon
Area: 8A Thai Van Lung Street, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Little Japan Town Saigon is a unique district located at the intersection of Le Thanh Ton and Thai Van Lung Streets in District 1, often dubbed the "Little Tokyo" of the city. This area perfectly recreates a Japanese atmosphere with its narrow alleys adorned with lanterns, wooden-tiled roofs, and signage featuring Japanese characters. The street is home to over 70 establishments, primarily Japanese-style restaurants, Izakaya pubs, spas, and convenience stores. The quarter is well-known for its quiet, clean, and civilized ambiance, offering a stark contrast to Saigon's hustle and bustle, making visitors feel as though they have stepped into Tokyo or Kyoto.

Name: Van Phat Temple
Area: 66/14 Nghia Thuc Street, Ward 5, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Van Phat Temple is a prominent temple of the Chinese community in District 5 (Cho Lon area), originally established in 1959. Though modest in size, the pagoda features a typical Chinese architectural style and expands vertically across five floors. The temple holds a Vietnamese record for housing over 10,000 Buddha statues of various sizes displayed throughout its halls, fitting its name, "Ten Thousand Buddhas." Notably, the main hall on the top floor offers an awe-inspiring view of the immense and intricate system of statues. At night, the temple is brightly illuminated by red lanterns, creating a mystical, warm, and unique atmosphere, drawing both Buddhists and visitors seeking tranquility.

Name: Ong Pagoda
Area: 678 Nguyen Trai Street, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Chua Ong (or Nghia An Assembly Hall) is a national architectural and artistic relic, constructed in the mid-18th century by the Teochew Chinese community in Saigon. The temple is primarily dedicated to Guan Yu (Quan Cong), the legendary general symbolizing loyalty and righteousness. The architecture is distinctly Teochew style, dominated by red and gold colors, intricate ceramic reliefs, and refined wood carving art. With its sacred, ancient atmosphere and a large central courtyard (San Thien Tinh), the Assembly Hall serves not only as a cultural and spiritual center for the Chinese community but also as an ideal destination to explore the history and cultural blend of Vietnamese and Chinese heritage in Cho Lon.

Name: Quan Am Temple
Area: 5 Lao Tu Street, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Quan Am Pagoda (also known as On Lang Assembly Hall) is an ancient temple established by the Fujian Chinese community in Saigon during the 19th century. The temple is primarily dedicated to the Goddess of Mercy, Quan The Am Bodhisattva, and is renowned for its sacredness and unique architecture, bearing the hallmarks of traditional Fujian style. The structure is distinguished by its curved tile roofs, exquisite ceramic reliefs, and especially the numerous paper lanterns hanging throughout the halls, creating a solemn and intimate atmosphere. Situated in the heart of Chinatown, Quan Am Pagoda serves not only as a religious site but also as a vibrant architectural museum, drawing visitors to admire its beauty and ancient cultural and spiritual significance.

Name: Ong Bon Temple
Area: 264 Hai Thuong Lan Ong Street, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Chua Ong Bon (formally Nhi Phu Temple) is one of the oldest temples in Saigon, established in the late 17th century by the Fujian Chinese community. The temple is primarily dedicated to Ong Bon (also known as Bon Dau Cong), the deity revered as the protector of the land and the community's safety. The architecture is highly traditional Fujian style, notable for its curved tiled roofs, vibrant ceramic relief decorations, and exquisite wood carving craftsmanship. Chua Ong Bon serves not only as a spiritual hub for the Fujian people but also as a precious architectural and artistic relic, remaining a sacred and ancient landmark within the bustling Cho Lon Chinatown.

Name: Thien Hau Temple
Area: 710 Nguyen Trai Street, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Thien Hau Temple (or Tue Thanh Guildhall) is one of the oldest and most sacred temples belonging to the Chinese community in Cho Lon, dating back to around 1760. The temple is dedicated to Thien Hau Thanh Mau (Mazu), the Goddess of the Sea, holding profound spiritual significance for Chinese immigrants. Its architecture showcases a classical Chinese style, notably featuring gracefully curved tiled roofs, colorful ceramic reliefs, and valuable large incense burners. The temple is famous for the distinctive coils of incense hanging from the ceiling, creating an atmospheric, ancient, and mystical space. It is a must-visit cultural landmark for exploring the unique architecture and heritage of Saigon's Chinese residents.

Name: Les Rives – Authentic River Experience

The company focuses on providing authentic experiences, allowing visitors to immerse themselves in local life, discover the Can Gio Mangrove Forest, and venture into remote backwaters. With its professional, well-organized service and knowledgeable guides, Les Rives offers an effective and memorable journey into Vietnam's natural beauty and heritage.

Name: Thien Ton Pagoda
Area: 117/3/2 An Binh Street, Ward 5, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Thien Ton Pagoda is a famous ancient temple nestled peacefully within an alley in District 5, recognized as a City-level Historical Relic. Established in 1947, the pagoda is distinguished by its traditional Vietnamese architecture, featuring intricate carvings, solemn altars, and a refreshing green courtyard. Notably, Thien Ton Pagoda holds significant historical importance: it secretly served as a revolutionary base, sheltering high-ranking officials of the Saigon - Gia Dinh Special Zone during the war for independence. Today, the pagoda is not only a place for worship and spiritual practice but also actively engages in charity and humanitarian activities, preserving both cultural and spiritual values.

Area: 100/15 Hung Vuong Street, Ward 9, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City 700000, Vietnam
Overview: UC Spaces is a lively board-game café in District 5 that blends a creative social atmosphere with great drinks. Guests can enjoy coffee, tea, and snacks while exploring a wide variety of board games — from strategy and party games to casual fun for beginners. With its modern design, friendly staff, and vibrant community, UC Spaces is an ideal hangout spot for game lovers and friend groups looking for a fun and cozy time together.

Name: Boom Music Box – Hung Vuong Branch
Area: 335 Hung Vuong Street, Ward 9, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City 700000, Vietnam
Overview: Boom Music Box – Hung Vuong Branch is a lively karaoke café and music lounge located in District 5. With vibrant lighting, fun décor, and private singing rooms, it’s a perfect spot for groups to hang out, celebrate, or simply enjoy singing their favorite songs. The atmosphere is energetic yet cozy, making it a great place to relax and have fun after work or on the weekend.

Name: Thu Do Market
Area: 220 Phung Hung Street, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Thu Do Market (officially Phung Hung Market) is one of the oldest and most bustling markets in District 5, established in 1928 and deeply connected to the Chinese community in Cho Lon. The market is famous for its two distinct sessions: The Morning session specializes in fresh, high-quality groceries and produce, earning it the nickname the "Rich People's Market." The Afternoon session transforms into a culinary heaven with distinctive Chinese-influenced street food like ha cao (dumplings), stir-fried noodles (hu tieu xao), bitter melon stuffed with fish paste, and the famous Ba Lu Vietnamese drip coffee. Cho Thu Do is a vibrant, authentic slice of life, preserving the century-old cultural and culinary heritage of Saigon's Chinese residents.

Name: Chinatown
Area: 165 Hai Thuong Lan Ong Street, Ward 13, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Saigon Chinatown, also known as Cho Lon, is the vibrant cultural heart of Ho Chi Minh City’s Chinese community. The area is filled with traditional shops, herbal medicine stores, temples, and food stalls offering authentic Chinese-Vietnamese cuisine. Visitors can explore colorful streets, unique architecture, and the bustling daily life that has defined this historic district for generations.

Name: Hao Si Phuong Alley
Area: 206 Tran Hung Dao B Street, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: Hao Si Phuong Alley is a century-old residential lane that preserves the charm of old-Saigon Chinatown. Known for its pastel-colored buildings, hanging lanterns, and vintage balconies, this narrow alley offers visitors a glimpse into the daily life of the local Chinese-Vietnamese community. A peaceful yet picturesque hidden spot for slow walks and photography.

Name: Master Escape
Area: 226 Tran Phu Street, Ward 9, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City.
Overview: Master Escape Room in District 5 offers immersive escape-room experiences with richly themed rooms including horror, thriller and mystery genres. Each game challenges groups with clever puzzles, high quality sets and engaging storylines, making it an exciting outing for friends or families.

Name: Karaoke ICOOL
Area: 878 Nguyen Trai Street, Ward 14, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam.
Overview: Karaoke ICOOL is a trendy and stylish venue in Quận 5 with modern design, ambient lighting, and high-quality audio. It’s well suited for both casual hangouts and more special occasions.

Name: The Convoy Café
Area: 175 Tran Hung Dao Street, Ward 11, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: The Convoy Café is a small, nostalgic coffee shop tucked along Tran Hung Dao Street in District 5. Its playful retro décor — featuring classic toys, comics and vintage memorabilia — gives off a warm, homey atmosphere. It’s a cozy place for coffee lovers and pop-culture fans to relax, chat, or enjoy a calm afternoon.

Name: The Muse Café
Area: 809/9 Tran Hung Dao Street, Ward 1, District 5, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: The Muse Café is a hidden gem in a quiet alley of District 5, offering a peaceful and minimalist atmosphere. Its clean design, soft lighting, and gentle background music make it ideal for reading, studying, or reflective conversations. A cozy, artistic space for those seeking calm moments away from the city noise.

Name: Quoc Thanh Cinestar Cinema
Area: 271 Nguyen Trai Street, Nguyen Cu Trinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam
Overview: The complex at 271 Nguyen Trai is a prominent multi-functional location in central District 1, known for housing Cinestar Quoc Thanh – a cinema with a long history, having once been a famous Vietnamese traditional opera theater . This address is also home to Quoc Thanh Wedding Center, specializing in luxurious and romantic wedding receptions and events. The area further attracts visitors with popular eateries like Bun Cha Pho Hang Quat, which serves authentic Hanoi-style noodle soup, alongside various coffee shops, making it a bustling destination for dining and entertainment right in the heart of the city.

Name: Me In's Kitchen
Area: 136/9 Le Thanh Ton Street, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Vietnam
Overview: Bep Me In (Mama In's Kitchen) is a renowned traditional Vietnamese restaurant nestled in a quiet alley near Ben Thanh Market. This hidden gem has been consistently recognized in the MICHELIN Guide Bib Gourmand list (since 2023), confirming its commitment to good quality and great value. The restaurant promotes itself as "Mama's kitchen with a twist," specializing in comforting Vietnamese family dishes that evoke childhood memories and warmth. Diners often praise signature items like the Banh Xeo (Vietnamese pancake with shrimp and pork, served with fresh herbs) and the unique Com trai dua (fried rice served in a coconut shell). With its decor featuring vivid yellow walls and blue shutters reminiscent of village houses, Bep Me In offers a welcoming and distinct dining experience.

Name: Home Saigon Restaurant
Area: 185/28 Pham Ngu Lao Street, Pham Ngu Lao Ward, District 1, Vietnam
Overview: HOME Saigon Restaurant is an upscale Vietnamese dining establishment, renowned for elevating traditional dishes to a new level through refinement and perfection in preparation. Situated in an elegant and luxurious setting, often within a classic Saigon villa, HOME Saigon embodies the culinary philosophy of "Comfort Food." The restaurant is designed with a harmonious blend of classic and modern aesthetics, creating an intimate atmosphere perfect for private parties or special events. HOME Saigon is an ideal destination for an immersive journey into Vietnam's culinary heritage, enjoyed within a high-class yet nostalgic setting.
